title: Helios Aero maintenance deployment capture
body:
Context / quick summary:
- Customer: Helios Aero (third-party MRO for regional carriers). They want an on-prem/private deployment in hangar network with periodic uplink windows (nightly sync).
- Primary use case: interactive tech support assistant for mechanics (short prompts, lookups, step-by-step procedures), plus nightly batch QA/embedding refresh for parts search.
- Hard constraints: no persistent PII exfil, no continuous cloud egress during work hours; ability to run air-gapped for cert audits.

Call notes (2025-01-15 kickoff):
- Stakeholders on call: Chris (Head of Ops), Priya (Lead Mechanic), Raj (IT security), + SEs Tom/Lina.
- Raj: requirement -> HSM-backed key management (on-prem KMS) and audit logs forwarded to their SIEM.
- Priya: mechanics will paste snippets from OEM manuals and upload small PDFs (1-3MB) as attachments to chat. Must retain numbering/format for procedures.
- Concern: deterministic text for compliance (they need reproducible recommended steps for safety sign-off).
- Ops: network is intermittent; some hangars have only 4G backups. They want local inference first, cloud fallback only during maintenance windows.

Technical gotchas we surfaced:
- Tokenization mismatch: OEM PDFs have weird unicode and bullet markers; need a preprocessor stage (strip odd bullets, preserve step numbers).
- Long-context recall: some procedures reference earlier sections ~6k tokens away. Quantized 4-bit model showed recall loss in bench tests — may need extended context or KV-cache disk-backed hot-start.
- Batch sizes: user interactions are typically 1–3 short queries; batching yields little gain and risks added latency. We should optimize for continuous batching disabled for interactive SLOs <300ms.
- Embedding freshness: they want nightly rebuilds tied to part catalog updates; embeddings must be pinned to model version for audit.
- Attachments: need OCR + text extraction pipeline inside their VPC. OCR errors change tokenization and hurt QA recall.

Proposed architecture (working):
1) Private control plane (Redwood Private) in their VPC; inference nodes on local GPU hosts (A10G for cost, H100 for heavy recalls) depending on hangar cluster size.
2) Local KMS + HSM integration; no plaintext keys leave their network.
3) Prefix/KV cache warmup daemon that pulls recent procedures overnight to NVMe-backed cache for sub-50ms warm starts.
4) Attachment ingestion service (OCR -> sanitizer -> tokenizer normalization) running on a small CPU pool.
5) Fallback policy: local inference preferred; if node unavailable and during nightly window -> route to Redwood hosted for batch jobs only (explicit opt-in per window).

Open questions / unknowns (action items below):
- Compliance: what exact determinism threshold acceptable? Do they require seed/temperature=0 and model checksum logged? (Ask legal/compliance: Raj)
- HSM: which vendor & API (Thales vs AWS CloudHSM local)? Need integration checklist. (Tom)
- Hardware procurement: hangar power/thermal limits — can we get GPU cards list and rack specs? (Ops to provide)
- OCR: are OEM manuals available as searchable PDFs or scans? Need sample docs to test tokenization. (Priya to send)
- Offline updates: how will embedding refresh artifacts be transported to air-gapped clusters? (S3 mirror + signed bundle?)

Immediate next steps and owners:
- Aisha: run two microbench kernels on A10G vs H100 configs with customer sample text (deliver by 2025-01-20).
- Tom: draft KMS/HSM integration notes and API checklist; propose vault flow (due 2025-01-21).
- Lina: prototype OCR+sanitizer pipeline using Tesseract + unicode normalizer; send tokenizer-diff report (due 2025-01-24).
- Priya: upload 5 sample procedures (real OEM pages, redacted) to secure share (by 2025-01-18).
- Raj: confirm SIEM log format and retention requirements (by 2025-01-22).

Risk profile / mitigations:
- Risk: degraded recall with quantized models -> Mitigation: maintain a backward-compatible FP16 variant for critical procedures; use rollouts with canary & auto-fallback.
- Risk: egress/policy violation during cloud fallback -> Mitigation: strict time-window toggles, signed approval by their IT, per-route gating in control plane.
- Risk: OCR-induced instruction corruption -> Mitigation: human-in-loop verification for first 100 procedures and automated QA metrics (BLEU-ish + rule checks).

Evaluation plan (proposal):
- Bench: retrieval-augmented QA on their sample set (n=250 procedures) measuring exact-step recall at top-1 and top-5.
- Regression detection: baseline from FP16 run; any quantized rollout must pass threshold >=95% of baseline exact-step recall.
- Latency SLO: interactive p95 <300ms for short queries (token length <128). Nightly batch latency unconstrained but throughput target 1000s of embeddings per hour.

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Watch for tokenization issues around OEM "§" markers and trademark symbols — library mapping needed.
- Consider adding a small local LRU cache of embeddings for most searched parts to avoid nightly cold starts.
- Might recommend model family with explicit denoising head or deterministic sampling support.

Meeting artifacts / follow-ups:
- Schedule in-person hangar visit week of 2025-02-03 (ops request).
- Create GH issue to track HSM integration and attach Tom's checklist: GH issue created: redwood-inference/private-deploy-helm#88.
- Draft customer-facing one-pager describing air-gap sync flow + emergency cloud fallback (Aisha to draft).

-- end of scratchpad --
